problem: The vast majority of containers report a 'warning' state with NaN memory readings, indicating a widespread stats collection or container lifecycle failure rather than isolated app issues.
possibleCauses: Docker daemon stats API failing to return valid metrics for stopped/paused/exited containers
Containers are in a non-running state (created/exited/restarting) causing NaN memory stats
Monitoring agent losing connection to Docker socket or cgroup stats interface
Host memory pressure (84%) and disk usage (85%) causing cgroup/stats subsystem instability
Docker daemon or containerd degraded, unable to report per-container resource usage
recommendations: Check actual container states via docker ps -a to confirm which are running vs exited/created
Restart the monitoring/stats collection agent or Docker daemon if stats API is unresponsive
Investigate high memory (84%) and disk (85%) usage on host to rule out resource exhaustion causing instability
Prune unused/stopped containers and volumes to free disk space
Isolate and inspect one representative warning container's logs and inspect output to identify root cause
Set up alerting threshold review since near-total warning state suggests monitoring pipeline issue, not per-app failure

problem: Application cannot connect to PostgreSQL database on localhost port 5432
possibleCauses: PostgreSQL service is not running or crashed
Postgres is bound to a different interface/port or config misconfigured
Database container not started or exited
Firewall or socket permission blocking local connection
recommendations: Check PostgreSQL service/container status and restart if stopped
Verify postgresql.conf listen_addresses and port settings
Inspect Postgres logs for crash or startup errors
Check disk space and resource limits that could cause DB crash
